title: Slalom Flex (Project Based) Data Engineer- Databricks
description:
Data Engineer- Databricks

Location: Remote – CST Hours
Employment Type: Full-Time Consultant
Duration: Project Based Contract Through End of Year with Likely Extension

Working Hours- 12:00 AM – 9:00 AM Central Time (CT) M-F.

Compensation- $30-35/hr

About Us

Slalom is a purpose-led, global business and technology consulting company. From strategy to implementation, our approach is fiercely human. In six+ countries and 43+ markets, we deeply understand our customers—and their customers—to deliver practical, end-to-end solutions that drive meaningful impact. Backed by close partnerships with over 400 leading technology providers, our 10,000+ strong team helps people and organizations dream bigger, move faster, and build better tomorrows for all. We’re honored to be consistently recognized as a great place to work, including being one of Fortune’s 100 Best Companies to Work For seven years running. Learn more at Slalom.com.

About the Role

Slalom’s Enhance & Operate (E&O) team is looking for a hands-on Data Engineer who enjoys building and improving data pipelines and keeping production platforms running smoothly. In this role, you’ll support a modern Databricks + Snowflake + Azure Data Factory (ADF) Enterprise Data Warehouse (EDW) ecosystem, combining data engineering fundamentals with operational excellence—monitoring pipelines, resolving incidents, developing code enhancements, and continuously improving reliability and performance in a service-oriented environment. 

You’ll work with a highly collaborative, cross-regional delivery model (“all-shore”) and partner closely with both technical and non-technical stakeholders. 

 

Work schedule: This role is working a shift between approximately 12:00 AM – 9:00 AM Central Time (CT).

 

What You’ll Do 
• Build, enhance, and troubleshoot Azure Data Factory (ADF) pipelines and Snowflake ELT/ETL processes, and Databricks ELT/ETL. 
• Monitor daily/weekly/monthly data batch cycles and respond quickly to job failures, latency, or data-quality issues. 
• Diagnose and resolve production incidents within Service-Level Agreements (SLA) targets using SQL, Python, platform logs, documentation, and runbooks. 
• Perform root cause analysis (RCA), write documentation of findings, and implement fixes to prevent recurrence of issues. 
• Drive operational improvements: automation, alert tuning, performance optimization, and reliability enhancements. 
• Work within ITIL/ITSM workflows (ticketing, incident/problem management, change processes) and communicate clearly with both technical and business stakeholders. 
• Collaborate with teammates across regions—sharing context early, documenting decisions, and maintaining strong handoffs. 
• Apply agentic AI in day-to-day E&O delivery using Snowflake Cortex and agentic coding tools to investigate incidents, accelerate root cause analysis, navigate code and data context, automate repeatable work, and turn operational knowledge into reusable skills. 
• Use agentic tools to support, not replace, engineering judgment by verifying evidence, challenging recommendations, protecting production data, and clearly communicating what the agent did, what was validated, and what still requires human approval. 

 

What You Bring 
• A proactive, data platform service-focused mindset: you will own incidents, issues, and development work end-to-end and follow your work through to resolution. 
• A Problem-solving mindset; Willingness to learn and understand how issues and resolutions fit into the EDW system design 
• Experience in working independently on assigned work; but also, comfortable collaborating with others to investigate and resolve issues; comfortable sharing concepts and information about issue resolution with teammates 
• 2-3 years of experience in data engineering, ETL/ELT development, or production support for data platforms. 
• Strong SQL skills (debugging, performance awareness, data validation). 
• Strong Python skills (troubleshooting, scripting, automation). 
• Hands-on experience with Snowflake and/or Databricks and Azure Data Factory (ADF). 
• Comfort working in a fast-paced, consulting-oriented environment where priorities shift and outcomes matter. 
• An agentic-assisted engineering mindset: comfort using AI agents as part of daily engineering work by providing clear context and constraints, reviewing proposed plans, SQL, and code, validating outputs against source evidence, and iterating when results are incomplete or unsafe. Prior Snowflake Cortex experience is not required. 
• Strong engineering fundamentals for AI-enabled operations, including Git and pull-request practices, scripting or Python experience, API and integration literacy, and the ability to trace issues across data pipelines, logs, code repositories, and operational records. 

 

Nice to have 
• Experience with ServiceNow, Control-M, Azure DevOps, Git-based workflows, and/or CI/CD. 
• Exposure to data observability/monitoring patterns, alerting, and platform logging. 
• Familiarity with modern data tooling (e.g., dbt) or cloud data ecosystem patterns. 
• Experience with Snowflake Cortex or enterprise GenAI platforms, including Cortex Agents, Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst, LLM functions, or a comparable enterprise agent or GenAI platform. 
• Experience building reusable agent solutions, including agent skills, tool integrations, prompts, or automations for repeatable engineering and operations workflows. 
• Experience with responsible AI operations, including retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) or governed knowledge, evaluation and observability, access controls, human-in-the-loop approvals, and safe production rollout. 

 

What success looks like (first 3–6 months) 
• You can independently troubleshoot common ADF/Snowflake/Databricks failures and stabilize recurring issues. 
• You consistently meet incident response expectations and communicate status clearly. 
• You deliver at least a few measurable improvements (automation, reduced failures, faster recovery, better monitoring). 
• You’re a trusted partner to teammates and stakeholders—reliable, proactive, and collaborative. 

Compensation and Benefits

Slalom prides itself on helping team members thrive in their work and life. As a result, Slalom is proud to invest in benefits that include meaningful time off and paid holidays, 401(k) with a match, a range of choices for highly subsidized health, dental, & vision coverage, adoption and fertility assistance, and long-term disability. We also offer yearly $350 reimbursement account for any well-being-related expenses.

Slalom is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. For this position, the base salary pay range is $30-35/hr. Actual compensation will depend upon an individual’s skills, experience, qualifications, location, and other relevant factors. The salary pay range is subject to change and may be modified at any time.

EEO and Accommodations

Slalom is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to inclusion, diversity, and equity in the workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration

for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. Slalom will also consider qualified applications with criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements.

Slalom welcomes and encourages applications from individuals with disabilities. Reasonable accommodations are available for candidates during all aspects of the

selection process. Please advise the talent acquisition team if you require accommodations during the interview process.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Backend — Booking Platform & APIs
description:
About ResortPass

ResortPass is redefining what it means to be a hotel guest. We give people daytime access to pools, beaches, spas, cabanas, and other hotel experiences without an overnight stay.

We work with more than 2,700 hotel partners across 30 countries. We have served more than 7 million guests and generated hundreds of millions of dollars for our hotel partners. Marriott has signed a global agreement with ResortPass, and Hilton has expanded its partnership with us.

We have proven the demand. Now we are building the booking and distribution platform that can bring hotel experiences to many more guests, categories, and channels.

Why this role matters

Most travel platforms are built around overnight rooms. ResortPass is building the platform for everything else a hotel can offer.

A day pass is sold by capacity. A cabana is reserved as a unit. A massage needs a time slot, provider, or room. Events have tickets. Food and beverage may be a product, an add-on, or part of a bundle. Each category has different rules for pricing, inventory, fulfillment, and cancellation.

We need one clear booking domain that supports these differences without creating a separate system for every category. That same inventory must be available through ResortPass, hotel systems, distribution partners, and authorized booking agents.

We are hiring a Senior Software Engineer to lead the technical work and be the primary hands-on builder for the ResortPass API. In your first year, multiple distribution partners and an authorized AI agent should complete real bookings through the same versioned API.

You will evolve a production Rails and Postgres booking system used by millions of guests. The hard work is keeping prices and inventory correct, preventing overselling, surviving retries and partial failures, and reconciling systems when they disagree.

Your ownership and team

You will own the API’s day-to-day technical roadmap and design decisions. In this hands-on individual contributor role, you will write production code, lead focused designs, guide migrations, and operate what you build. You will partner with our Staff Engineer on foundational domain and architecture choices.

You will be the primary builder, but you will not work alone. Other backend engineers will contribute and build supply, PMS, and POS connectors using the patterns you establish. Product, Partnerships, and hotel operations will work with you from requirements through production launch.

This is one of our highest-impact technical bets. What you build will determine how quickly ResortPass can enter new booking channels and categories.

This role works from our NYC headquarters four days per week. The base salary range is $190,000–$210,000, plus equity, based on experience.

What You’ll Do

• Build and launch the external ResortPass API. Define stable, versioned contracts for live pricing, availability, holds, booking creation, changes, and cancellations.
• Make booking operations safe under real failures. Design idempotency, recovery, webhooks, and reconciliation for retries, timeouts, duplicates, and partial success.
• Evolve the core booking domain. Create clear models and invariants for products, schedules, prices, inventory, holds, carts, and bookings.
• Make the platform extensible. Prove that a new category such as events or food and beverage can use the shared booking model instead of requiring a separate system.
• Own the architecture for supply, PMS, and POS integrations. Create reusable connector patterns so other engineers can add partners without reinventing failure handling and reconciliation.
• Define the data contracts that keep inventory discoverable through OpenSearch. Search is supporting technology for this role, not its primary ownership area.
• Operate what you build. Set reliability and latency targets, and add the tests, metrics, dashboards, alerts, tracing, and runbooks needed for a critical booking path.
• Turn partner needs into durable platform capabilities, explain tradeoffs clearly, and raise the engineering bar through practical reviews and mentoring.

How We Ship

We move quickly by building quality from the start. A change is done when it is tested, deployed, observable, and safe to roll back. We use AI tools aggressively, but engineers remain accountable for architecture, correctness, and production outcomes.

Explore engineering at ResortPass, including why we work and what we are building next.

Tech stack

• Backend: Ruby on Rails, Node.js
• Data: Postgres, MongoDB
• Search: OpenSearch
• APIs and integrations: REST, OpenAPI, webhooks
• Infrastructure and observability: AWS, Datadog
• Testing: RSpec, Playwright

Who You Are

We encourage candidates to apply even if they do not match every line below.

• You have 6+ years of software engineering experience, or a track record of equivalent impact.
• You have designed transactional systems, built external APIs or integration platforms, and safely evolved data models in production.
• You understand relational modeling, concurrency, consistency, asynchronous workflows, and distributed failures.
• You turn complex business rules into clear boundaries, lifecycle states, contracts, and invariants.
• You can lead an important system as its primary builder while collaborating on foundational decisions.
• You care about correctness, testing, observability, and safe rollouts.
• You communicate directly, listen well, and improve the work of engineers around you.

Ruby on Rails experience is useful, but not required. Experience with marketplaces, reservations, inventory-constrained commerce, public APIs, or third-party booking systems is also helpful. We care most about your backend judgment, track record, and ability to learn.

What Success Looks Like In 6–12 Months

• Multiple distribution partners and an authorized AI agent complete real bookings through one reusable API.
• The full booking lifecycle meets agreed targets for correctness, success rate, latency, overselling, recovery, and reconciliation.
• Reusable contracts and connector patterns materially reduce the work required to onboard the next partner.
• The shared booking model supports at least one new category without a separate booking system.

As the API becomes a company-wide platform, this role can grow toward Staff through demonstrated impact across the booking domain, integrations, and distribution.

Benefits

• Health, dental, and vision coverage, with ResortPass contributing to monthly premiums
• Stock options
• 401(k) plan
• Unlimited paid time off
• Paid parental leave
• Annual ResortPass credit for pools, beaches, spas, and other experiences

description:
A World-Changing Company

Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

The Role

Software Engineers at Palantir build software at scale to transform how organizations around the world use data. In this role, you’ll have an opportunity to grow more quickly than you ever envisioned as you contribute high-quality code directly to Palantir Gotham: products that are deployed at some of the most important institutions across the government, defense and non-profit sectors . You'll create features used by research scientists, aerospace engineers, intelligence analysts, and economic forecasters in countries around the world. Palantir's Product Development organization is made up of small teams of Software Engineers, each focusing on a specific aspect of a product. For example, you might join a team that builds geospatial mapping tools for mission critical operations, or a component of the Gotham release infrastructure. We encourage communication and collaboration among teams to share context, skills, and experience, so you'll also have the opportunity to learn about other business areas.

Core Responsibilities

As a Software Engineer, you are involved throughout the product lifecycle - from idea generation, design, and prototyping, to execution and shipping, all while also being paired with a mentor dedicated to your growth and success. You'll collaborate closely with technical and non-technical counterparts to understand our customers' problems and build products that tackle them. One of the most effective ways to understand what our users need is to meet them. You may receive an opportunity to tour the assembly line at an auto-manufacturer or join a counter-terror analyst at their desk to really understand their mission and difficulties.

SWE Principles Include

• Ownership: We see projects through from beginning to end in spite of obstacles we may encounter.
• Collaboration: We work internally with people from a variety of backgrounds — such as other Software Engineers, Product Managers, Designers and Product Reliability Engineers. We also partner with our business development teams (Forward Deployed Engineers, Deployment Strategists) in order to understand and solve our customers' problems.
• Trust: We trust each other to effectively handle time and priorities, and don't micromanage. We want people to have the space to think for themselves, while feeling supported by their team.

Technologies We Use

Skills

It doesn’t matter what languages you know when you join us; what matters is that you can write clean, effective code and learn new languages quickly. Our software is constantly evolving, so we need engineers who can do the same. Alongside peers that bring diverse experience - whether you’re a former university Teaching Assistant, switched to computer science recently, or are a hackathon enthusiast — you'll build your skills to apply the best technology to solve a given problem. Right now, we use:

• A variety of languages, including Java and Go for backend and Typescript for frontend
• Open-source technologies like Cassandra, Spark, Elasticsearch, React, and Redux
• Industry-standard build tooling, including Gradle and GitHub

What We Value

• Ability to communicate and collaborate with a variety of individuals, including engineers, users and non-technical team members.
• Willingness to learn and make decisions independently, and the ability to ask questions effectively.

What We Require

• Active US Security clearance or eligibility and willingness to obtain a US Security clearance.
• Engineering background in fields such as Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, and Physics.
• Familiarity with data structures, storage systems, cloud infrastructure, front-end frameworks, and other technical tools.
• Experience coding in programming languages, such as Java, C++, Python, JavaScript, or similar languages.

To Apply, Please Submit The Following

• An updated resume / CV - please do so in PDF format.
• Thoughtful responses to our application questions.

Salary

The estimated salary range for this position is estimated to be $145,000 - $155,000/year. Money is being rewritten to run on AI agents - systems that initiate, authorize, and settle transactions with no human in the loop. title: Lead Full-Stack Engineer (React Native + Postgres)
description:
SparqList — NYC (hybrid) · Full-time · $160K–$210K + meaningful early-stage equity

About SparqList

SparqList is a local-discovery marketplace launching in New York City — the deals, perks, and experiences worth leaving the house for, at the places locals actually love. It's a three-sided product connecting consumers, creators, and local businesses, with real money moving through it: redemptions, event tickets, gift cards, vendor credits, and creator payouts.

The product is built and entering App Store review. It was designed and shipped at very high velocity, and we're now bringing on engineering leadership so it can scale safely beyond its solo-founder origins.

The role

You'll be the first engineering hire and the technical anchor for the entire platform. This is a senior, full-stack, backend-heavy role. You'll own the mobile app, the admin dashboard, and — most importantly — the custom Postgres backend and the money layer. If we hire one engineer, it's you, and you'll help hire the team that comes next.

This is a build-and-harden role, not a greenfield one. The system already exists and works; your job is to own it, make it safe to operate, and keep it moving.

What you'll own
• A production React Native app (Expo SDK 54): ~148 screens, 149 components, 13 state stores, ~163K lines.
• A large custom Postgres backend: ~101 tables, ~457 database functions (RPCs), ~331 row-level security policies, ~41 edge functions, and 600+ migrations.
• A 22-page admin dashboard (~21K lines).
• The money layer: Stripe + RevenueCat (Apple IAP), integer-cents ledgers, escrow, and payouts — the most sensitive and least-forgiving part of the system.
• Establishing the engineering foundations the codebase doesn't have yet: automated testing, CI safety nets, and the practices that let a growing team ship without breaking money or security paths.

The honest reality (we'd rather you hear it now)

We believe in being straight with candidates:
• The codebase is large, well-documented, and disciplined about security and migrations — but it has near-zero automated test coverage (a handful of test files across ~260K lines). Standing up a real test suite around the money and security paths is one of your first and most important mandates.
• A lot of system knowledge currently lives with the founder. Part of your early work is turning that tribal knowledge into shared, durable engineering practice.
• The workflow today is fast and lightly-branched. You'll bring the process maturity a money-moving product needs, without killing the velocity that got it here.

If "inherit a real, working, financially-sensitive system and make it bulletproof" excites you, this is a great role. If you need a pristine, fully-tested codebase to be productive, it isn't.

You're probably a fit if you have
• Strong full-stack experience with deep backend/database ownership — you're genuinely comfortable in Postgres (functions/RPCs, row-level security, migrations), not just calling an API.
• Real production React Native experience (Expo a strong plus).
• Experience building or operating payments/financial systems — ledgers, escrow, payouts, Stripe, and the care that money code requires (idempotency, reconciliation, integer-cents accounting, auditability).
• A track record of introducing testing and CI to under-tested codebases, and the judgment to prioritize the highest-risk paths first.
• Comfort being the senior technical owner — making architecture calls, operating in production, and eventually helping hire and mentor.

Bonus points
• Marketplace or multi-sided platform experience (supply + demand, matching, payouts).
• App Store release and mobile ops experience (builds, review, over-the-air updates, crash monitoring).
• Security-minded instincts around RLS, access control, and PII.
• Startup or founding-engineer experience where you owned a lot with little support.

Compensation
• $160K–$210K base, depending on experience, plus meaningful early-stage equity.
• Hybrid in New York City.

How to apply

Send a short note on a production system you've owned end-to-end. Ideally one involving payments or a database you were responsible for keeping correct — along with how you'd approach adding tests to a large, untested, money-moving codebase.

Links to relevant work welcome.

Job Description

The Software Engineer designs, develops, and maintains complex applications and embedded systems with minimal supervision, contributing to advanced test and simulation solutions for electronic warfare applications. Responsibilities
• Design, code, and maintain software applications in various programming languages with minimal supervision.

• Apply object-oriented design principles and design patterns to build scalable and maintainable software solutions.
• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to support test and simulation hardware and software for electronic warfare applications.

• Manage multiple tasks and projects simultaneously while meeting deadlines and demonstrating strong initiative.

• 4–5+ years of professional experience in C/C++ embedded programming; entry-level candidates will not be considered.

• Strong proficiency in embedded software development using C and C++ for microcontrollers and FPGAs.
• Experience working in Linux and embedded Linux environments.
• Hands-on experience with firmware development and debugging.
• Proficiency with lab equipment such as spectrum analyzers and digital oscilloscopes for debugging and validation.

• Knowledge of coding standards and the complete software development lifecycle.

• You'll join a team that's warm and grounded. People here help each other, share what they know, and take pride in leaving the codebase better than they found it.

• You'll be set up to succeed. We believe in sound patterns and good defaults so that doing the right thing is also the easy thing.

You will contribute directly to the design and implementation of data pipelines, transformations, and analytics-ready datasets across our Azure platform.
• Design, implement, and maintain reliable Azure-based data pipelines that support analytics, AI/ML, and enterprise integration use cases.
• Actively contribute code across the data platform — developing pipelines, writing transformations, optimizing SQL, and supporting production workloads.
• Own specific areas of the platform — pipelines, datasets, transformations, or integrations — ensuring quality, performance, and maintainability.
• Apply established patterns, frameworks, and standards to reinforce consistency and quality across the platform.
• Work closely with data engineers, analysts, product owners, and stakeholders to translate business requirements into effective technical solutions.

• 4+ years of hands-on experience engineering data pipelines and data platforms.
• Demonstrated experience building and maintaining cloud-based data solutions in Azure (or comparable cloud environments).
• Practical, hands-on exposure to data lakes, data marts, and data warehouses; data pipelines and orchestration; and modern ELT/ETL patterns.

• Experience with CI/CD pipelines for data platforms.
• Familiarity with Agile delivery and iterative development practices.
• Exposure to streaming, near-real-time data, or observability/monitoring for data systems.
• A genuine interest in continuous learning and technical growth within data engineering.

Full Stack Software Engineer, Lead

The Opportunity:

As a full stack developer, you can resolve a problem with a complete end-to-end solution in a fast, agile environment. If you’re looking for the chance to not just develop software, but to create a system that will make a difference, we need you on our team. We’re looking for an experienced developer like you with the skills needed to develop software and systems from vision to production ready.

This role is more than just coding. As a full stack developer at Booz Allen, you’ll use your passion to master new tools and techniques and identify needed system improvements. You’ll help clients overcome their most difficult challenges using the latest architectural approaches, tools, and technologies. You’ll make sure the solution developed by the team considers the current architecture and operating environment, as well as future functionality and enhancements.

The Lead Software Engineer supports the design development testing and deployment of complex software systems that support mission-critical operations. This role applies software engineering principles and SAFe Agile methodologies to deliver scalable secure and high-performance applications. The Lead Software Engineer supports cross functional team collaboration to ensure software solutions meet technical functional and security requirements throughout the lifecycle.

Join us. The world can't wait.

You Have:

• 8+ years of experience designing, modifying, developing, writing, and implementing software programming applications using agile methods
• 8+ years of experience in software development with basic programming languages, technologies, tools, or web development stacks
• Experience with Agile methodology, extreme programming, software engineering, product management, and software products
• Experience writing source code for new applications or generating and enhancing code samples for existing applications
• Experience using back-end and front-end languages to develop complete solutions
• Experience creating solutions to complex problems within a collaborative, cross-functional team
• Active TS/SCI clearance; willingness to take a polygraph exam
• Bachelor's degree or 8+ years of experience in software engineering in lieu of a degree

Nice If You Have:

• Experience acquiring client requirements and resolving workflow problems through automation optimization
• Experience with Java, Python, C#, C, C++, .NET, JavaScript, React, NodeJS, PHP, or Drupal
• Ability to work with automated testing tools to perform testing and maintenance
• Master’s degree

At Booz Allen, we celebrate your contributions, provide you with opportunities and choices, and support your total well-being. Our offerings include health, life, disability, financial, and retirement benefits, as well as paid leave, professional development, tuition assistance, work-life programs, and dependent care. title: Mechanical Engineer III - Medical Devices
description:
Mechanical Engineer III

Company: Sonablate Corp.
Location: Indianapolis, IN
Department: Engineering Operations
Reports To: Director, Hardware Development
Job Type: Full-Time, Permanent
FLSA Status: Exempt
Salary Range: $105,000 – $115,000 annually
Bonus: Eligible per company plan
Relocation: Not available
Anticipated Start Date: July 2026

About Sonablate

Sonablate Corp. is a medical technology company focused on high-intensity focused ultrasound, or HIFU, technology. Our work supports the design, development, manufacturing, and continuous improvement of medical devices used in a regulated healthcare environment.

We are looking for a Mechanical Engineer III to join our Engineering Operations team in Indianapolis. This role is ideal for an experienced mechanical engineer who enjoys solving technical problems, improving existing products, supporting manufacturing, and contributing to new product development within an FDA-regulated environment.

Position Summary

The Mechanical Engineer III is responsible for supporting both new and existing Sonablate products through mechanical design, product testing, engineering documentation, product investigations, design changes, and remediation activities.

This position will work cross-functionally with Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Regulatory, Clinical, Supply Chain, and Service teams. The Mechanical Engineer III will manage assigned projects from initiation through completion while working within Sonablate’s quality management system.

This role also serves as a senior technical resource and mentor to other members of the Engineering Operations team.

Key Responsibilities

• Provide technical support for existing and new products by developing mechanical engineering solutions with minimal supervision.

• Research, verify, and implement replacement components for end-of-life parts while maintaining current product design intent.

• Design parts, assemblies, systems, and sub-systems using SolidWorks.

• Support new product development, product improvements, design changes, and remediation activities.

• Generate and execute test protocols and prepare test reports.

• Develop and maintain engineering documentation, including:

• Bills of Material

• Engineering change requests

• Engineering files

• Supplier information

• User manuals

• Test specifications

• Design History Files

• Technical File documentation

• Develop jigs, tools, equipment, fixtures, and related instructions or documentation.

• Lead and support investigations related to CAPAs, customer complaints, manufacturing issues, and product performance concerns.

• Determine root cause and identify appropriate corrections and corrective actions.

• Assist Manufacturing with testing, troubleshooting, and production startup activities.

• Support project planning and execution to ensure timely completion of assigned engineering tasks.

• Present project status updates to stakeholders, management, and cross-functional teams.

• Follow policies and procedures required in an FDA-controlled environment.

• Serve as a mentor and technical advisor to junior engineering team members.

• Identify and support new technologies or process improvements that increase productivity and efficiency.

• Perform other duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree or advanced degree in Mechanical Engineering.

• 6–9 years of related mechanical engineering experience, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Strong experience with SolidWorks.

• Strong understanding of electro-mechanical systems.

• Knowledge of polymers, metals, and manufacturing methods or processes.

• Experience creating and maintaining engineering documentation.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Strong documentation practices and attention to detail.

• Ability to work cross-functionally in a regulated environment.

• Familiarity with tool shop equipment such as mills, lathes, drill presses, and small tools.

Preferred Qualifications

• Previous experience in medical device design.

• Experience working in an FDA-regulated or ISO 13485 environment.

• Experience with hardware/software interfacing.

• Experience supporting CAPAs, customer complaints, root cause investigations, and design remediation.

• Experience supporting products from development through commercialization and post-market support.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is a hands-on mechanical engineer who can move between design work, documentation, product testing, manufacturing support, and problem solving. This person should be comfortable working in a regulated environment, collaborating with multiple departments, and mentoring less experienced engineers.

Work Environment

This position is based in Indianapolis, Indiana, and supports engineering, manufacturing, quality, regulatory, and product support activities in a medical device environment.

Compensation

The salary range for this position is $105,000 to $115,000 annually, depending on experience and qualifications. This position is eligible for bonus consideration under the company’s bonus plan.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Sonablate Corp. is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected status.

title: Data Engineer Team Leader (Science/Engineering Program Manager 3)
description:
What You Will Do

Join our team at Los Alamos National Laboratory! The Weapons Research Services (WRS) Division's National Security Research Center (NSRC) is Los Alamos National Laboratory's classified library. The NSRC's lineage dates back to 1943 when it was formed as part of the Manhattan Project and houses 80+ years of scientific and engineering research, designs, procedures, and other reports. The NSRCMS group provides services for classified and historical research including training, tours, collection management, data engineering, knowledge management, project support and research assistance.

The NSRC is seeking an experienced and collaborative Data Engineering Team Leader to lead a team of data engineers responsible for partnering with scientific and engineering organizations to ensure research data are managed as long-term mission assets. This team serves as the bridge between data-generators and mission data repositories, helping customers implement sound data management practices that maximize the accessibility, quality, and long-term value of their data.

The Data Engineering Team Leader will provide technical and operational leadership for data management initiatives across multiple programs. This includes developing data strategies, guiding repository adoption, planning resources, negotiating budgets, overseeing project portfolios, and ensuring the team delivers high-quality customer support. The ideal candidate combines expertise in research data management with strong leadership, program management, and stakeholder engagement.

This challenging and exciting position requires a motivated and professional individual who is capable of quickly changing focus, acting independently, and thriving within a collaboratively defined scope of work. Scope is established in partnership with WRS leadership and weapons program customers to align with mission priorities, ensuring clear objectives while allowing flexibility to adapt as needs evolve. This includes working directly with weapons program stakeholders to validate requirements and deliverables. The role operates as the onsite team leader, administering work to the team in a semi-autonomous manner balancing initiative with accountability to organizational goals.

What You Need

Minimum Job Requirements:

Technical Knowledge: Demonstrated experience in managing scientific or engineering data throughout its lifecycle from creation through long-term preservation and reuse. Knowledge of research data management principles, including metadata, data quality, curation, provenance, preservation, and governance. Familiarity with recognized data management frameworks and best practices, including FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Interoperable, Reusable) principles and Certified Data Management Professional (CDMP) concepts. Ability to develop strategic approaches that improve organizational data maturity and maximize the long-term value of mission data.

Project Management: Demonstrated ability to convert concepts and strategic objectives into executable projects with measurable outcomes. Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously while balancing priorities and deadlines. Familiarity with coordinating interdisciplinary efforts and aligning project work with broader organizational goals. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail in both planning and execution.

Customer Relations and Stakeholder Engagement: Ability to build effective working relationships with both internal and external stakeholders. Experience collaborating with leadership, subject matter experts, partner organizations, and/or public audiences. Ability to assess customer needs and translate them into achievable projects scopes and deliverables. Experience setting realistic expectations regarding project scope, timelines, resources, and deliverables.
Leadership: Demonstrated ability to lead and develop a team through mentorship, guidance, and follow-up. Ability to plan, schedule, and assign work to others.

Teamwork/Collaboration: Demonstrated ability to foster a respectful, collaborative, and productive work environment. Ability to work constructively and professionally with colleagues across disciplines and backgrounds. Ability to collaborate and strategize with application product owners responsible for data platforms. Experience mentoring staff and supporting professional development. Willingness to share knowledge, provide constructive feedback, and support team success.

Clearance: This position requires the ability to obtain a DOE Q clearance, which typically requires US citizenship
Education/Experience: Position requires a bachelor's degree in a science or engineering related field from an accredited institution and 8 years of directly related technical and program management experience; or an equivalent combination of education and technical experience directly related to the occupation. At this level an advanced degree is typically expected.

Desired Qualifications:

• Knowledge of the LANL weapons programs and associated datasets.
• Advanced degree in Data Science, Information Science, Computer Science, Engineering, Library and Information Science, or related field.
• Certified Data Management Professional (CDMP) certification or similar.
• Experience with enterprise data governance, metadata standards, or data stewardship programs.

Work Location: The work location for this position is onsite and located in Los Alamos, NM. All work locations are at the discretion of management.

Position commitment: Regular appointment employees are required to serve a period of continuous service in their current position in order to be eligible to apply for posted jobs throughout the Laboratory. If an employee has not served the time required, they may only apply for Laboratory jobs with the documented approval of their Division Leader. The position commitment for this position is 1 year.

Note to Applicants:

For full consideration, applicants must submit a comprehensive cover letter that addresses all the minimum requirements of the position.

Due to federal restrictions contained in the current National Defense Authorization Act, citizens of the People's Republic of China-including the special administrative regions of Hong Kong and Macau-as well as citizens of the Islamic Republic of Iran, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (North Korea), and the Russian Federation, who are not Lawful Permanent Residents ("green card" holders) are prohibited from accessing facilities that support the mission, functions, and operations of national security laboratories and nuclear weapons production facilities, which includes Los Alamos National Laboratory.
Where You Will Work

Located in beautiful northern New Mexico, Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) is a multidisciplinary research institution engaged in strategic science on behalf of national security. Our generous benefits package includes:

§ PPO or High Deductible medical insurance with the same large nationwide network

§ Dental and vision insurance

title: Senior Software Engineer - Platform Engineer
description:
About Clear Street:

Clear Street’s mission is to give every sophisticated investor access to every asset, in every market, through a unified platform built for speed, transparency and scale.

We give our clients the technology, tools, and service once reserved for the largest institutions, rebuilt with modern infrastructure. Our single, cloud-native, end-to-end capital markets platform powers investor growth today and is transforming how they can interact with markets tomorrow.

For more information, visit https://clearstreet.io.

The Role

As a Platform Engineer, your customers are our engineers.

You'll build the internal platform that enables product teams to ship software faster, safer, and with greater confidence. Rather than simply managing infrastructure, you'll create self-service capabilities, intelligent automation, and reusable platform services that eliminate operational complexity and allow engineers to focus on building products.

You will partner closely with software engineers to understand friction in the development lifecycle and turn those pain points into scalable platform capabilities.

You'll work on problems like:

• Build self-service developer platforms that enable engineers to provision infrastructure, deploy applications, manage secrets, and access shared services with minimal operational overhead.
• Create reusable platform services and SDKs including identity & authorization, secrets management, deployment orchestration, service discovery, configuration management, and platform APIs.
• Design opinionated "golden paths" that make the easiest way also the best way for engineers to build, test, deploy, and operate software.
• Build intelligent CI/CD platforms that reduce deployment time, improve release confidence, and automate testing, security, and compliance.
• Improve developer workflows by investing in local development environments, faster build systems, ephemeral environments, and platform automation.
• Continuously measure and improve developer productivity through platform metrics, engineering insights, and workflow optimization.
• Collaborate with application teams to simplify software delivery, improve reliability, and remove operational toil through automation.
• Build platform capabilities that improve scalability, resiliency, observability, and operational excellence across the engineering organization.
• Champion Infrastructure as Code, GitOps, and platform engineering best practices while helping teams adopt modern engineering workflows.
• Experiment with emerging technologies, AI-assisted development, and developer tooling that transforms how engineers build software.

The Team

We believe great engineering organizations are built on great developer experiences. Our Platform Engineering team builds the internal products, services, and automation that every engineer depends on every day. We treat our platform as a product, with engineers as our customers and developer productivity as our north star.

Our mission is to remove friction from software delivery by creating intuitive, self-service platforms that make infrastructure invisible, deployments effortless, and operational excellence the default.

You'll work across every engineering team to understand their challenges, identify opportunities for automation, and build platform capabilities that scale with the organization. Whether it's reducing deployment time from hours to minutes, enabling one-click environment creation, or building reusable platform APIs, your work will have an immediate impact on every engineer at the company.

If you're passionate about building tools that thousands of engineering workflows depend on—and enjoy solving complex distributed systems problems while improving the daily lives of other engineers—you'll thrive here.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for engineers who enjoy building platforms rather than operating infrastructure.

You should have:

• 5+ years of experience in Platform Engineering, Software Engineering, Infrastructure Engineering, DevOps, or Site Reliability Engineering.
• Strong software engineering fundamentals with experience building production-quality software in Go, Python, Java, or similar languages.
• Experience designing developer platforms, internal tooling, automation frameworks, or shared engineering services.
• Deep understanding of cloud-native technologies, Kubernetes, Linux, containers, and distributed systems.
• Experience building modern CI/CD platforms and software delivery pipelines using tools such as GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, ArgoCD, Jenkins, or similar technologies.
• Experience with Infrastructure as Code using Terraform or comparable technologies.
• A product mindset—you think about usability, adoption, documentation, and developer experience when building internal platforms.
• Passion for automation and eliminating repetitive manual work.
• Strong communication skills and the ability to partner with engineering teams to understand problems and deliver scalable solutions.
• Curiosity to continuously explore emerging technologies, platform engineering practices, and AI-powered developer tooling.

The Technology You'll Work With

You'll build on a modern cloud-native platform that includes:

• Kubernetes
• AWS
• Terraform
• ArgoCD
• GitHub Actions
• Helm
• Kafka
• Temporal
• PostgreSQL
• Snowflake
• Datadog
• Go, Java, Python
• gRPC & Protobuf
• Tilt
• Internal Platform APIs and Developer Tooling

What Success Looks Like

Within your first year, you'll help create a platform that enables engineers to:

• Deploy services in minutes through self-service workflows.
• Provision infrastructure without opening support tickets.
• Spin up development environments on demand.
• Build and release software through standardized, automated pipelines.
• Resolve issues faster with best-in-class observability and diagnostics.
• Spend less time on operational tasks and more time delivering customer value.

Your impact won't be measured by the number of servers you manage—it will be measured by how much faster and happier our engineers become.

Which range a candidate fits into and where a candidate falls in the range will be based on job related factors such as relevant experience, skills, and location. These ranges represent Base Salary only, which is just one element of Clear Street's total compensation. The ranges stated do not include other factors of total compensation such as bonuses or equity.

Our belief has always been that we are better as a business when we are all together in person. We are requiring employees to be in the office 4 days per week. Our top priority is our people. We’re continuously investing in a culture that promotes collaboration. We help each other through challenges and celebrate each other's successes. title: Software Engineer, Mission Dev - U.S. Government
description:
About Nominal

Nominal is building the connected test and operations platform powering the world's most advanced hardware systems, from spacecraft and autonomous vehicles to next-generation defense programs. Our platform gives hardware engineering teams a single place to ingest data, analyze performance, automate test execution, and collaborate across every phase of development, so they can move faster without sacrificing safety or precision. We're a fast-moving team that owns problems end-to-end, works across disciplines, and thrives at the intersection of hardware and software.

We serve top-tier commercial and defense customers, from autonomy leaders like Anduril and Shield AI to next-generation aerospace teams like Hermeus and REGENT, and performance engineering teams like Pratt Miller Motorsports, alongside mission partners within the U.S. Navy and U.S. Air Force on programs where failure isn’t an option. We’re backed by Sequoia, General Catalyst, Founders Fund, Lux Capital, and Lightspeed. Our team draws from SpaceX, Palantir, Anduril, Applied Intuition, and other leading companies, united by a common mission: giving hardware engineers the tools to build the future with speed, safety, and confidence.

As a Software Engineer on the Mission Dev team, you will operate at the intersection of software engineering, customer deployment, and mission-critical government programs. You are not just shipping code — you are embedding with customers, deploying software into high-stakes environments, and owning outcomes from first integration to long-term success. You will bridge Nominal’s platform with real-world government applications across the Department of Defense, Department of Energy, NASA, and other U.S. government agencies.

This is a hybrid of software engineer, forward-deployed engineer, and technical program lead. You will write production-grade code, design integrations, manage deployments on government networks, and serve as a trusted technical advisor to mission operators. If you think like a startup founder, thrive in ambiguity, and want to see your code powering rocket test stands, autonomy labs, and mission-critical defense programs, Nominal is the place to do it.

🚀 About The Role

Mission Dev is one of the most unique roles at Nominal. You'll write production-grade code, embed with government customers on-site, and own the bridge between what our platform offers today and what a government program needs to succeed.

That might mean deploying Nominal onto a classified network for a Navy flight test squadron, building a custom telemetry pipeline for a DoD autonomy program, or standing up integrations at a NASA test facility, then watching an engineer use what you shipped yesterday and iterating on the spot. You'll work inside the constraints that come with federal environments: accreditation processes, air-gapped networks, strict cybersecurity requirements, and government acquisition timelines. The role requires someone who can deliver high-quality software without losing velocity in these environments.

Mission Devs are brought in when there's a specific technical gap to bridge. You might get looped in during pre-sales to integrate a program's data and demonstrate how Nominal fits their mission workflows, or you might be building program-specific tooling mid-deployment that evolves into a permanent product capability. The work you do for one program often becomes a core product used across our entire customer base — our video-alongside-telemetry capability, for example, started as a single customer need and is now a platform-wide feature. The "last 10%" looks different for every mission, and that's what makes the work compelling.

🔍 What We’re Looking For

• 5+ years of experience in software engineering, forward-deployed engineering, or a technical role that combined building with customer-facing work.
• Experience working with or inside U.S. Government agencies, particularly DoD, and with deploying software on U.S. government networks.
• Track record of shipping production software in dynamic or ambiguous environments.
• Strong systems thinking — you can understand complex technical ecosystems end-to-end.
• Clear communicator, comfortable writing technical documentation and presenting to executive stakeholders.
• Willingness to travel up to 50%.
• Curiosity about hardware systems and willingness to learn the physical domains our customers operate in.
• Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Top Secret clearance. Active clearance is a strong plus.

🎯 Why Nominal

• Mission-critical impact with top-tier government and commercial customers
• Backed by world-class investors
• Work alongside elite engineers from SpaceX, Palantir, Anduril, and more
• Build and deploy real systems powering rockets, aircraft, autonomous systems, and national security infrastructure

At Nominal, your code doesn’t sit in a demo environment — it powers real missions.

✨ Benefits/Perks

• 🏥 100% coverage of medical, dental, and vision insurance
• 🏖️ Unlimited PTO and sick leave
• 🍽️ Free lunch, snacks, and coffee
• 🚀 Professional Development Stipend
• 🛠️ In-office hardware lab with a $250 project stipend

title: Sr Data Engineer (Data Architecture and Modeling)
description:
#WeAreParamount on a mission to unleash the power of content… you in?
We’ve got the brands, we’ve got the stars, we’ve got the power to achieve our mission to entertain the planet – now all we’re missing is… YOU! Becoming a part of Paramount means joining a team of passionate people who not only recognize the power of content but also enjoy a touch of fun and uniqueness. Together, we co-create moments that matter – both for our audiences and our employees – and aim to leave a positive mark on culture.

Overview and Responsibilities:

The Signal Intelligence (SigInt) team turns a high-volume, multi-source data ecosystem — operational systems, client-app event streams, ad-tech platforms, stitcher events, ad server logs, and telemetry — into the trusted data models, metrics, and dashboards that drive business, product, and ad-ops decisions.

We are hiring a Senior Data Engineer who is, in equal measure, a data modeler, a SQL craftsperson, and an analyst — not only a pipeline builder. You will own data end-to-end: modeling raw events into conformed, analytics-ready marts; writing the analytical SQL that answers hard business questions; defining the metrics leadership relies on; and building the pipelines that feed it all. Because we sit close to the business, translating ambiguous questions into durable models and clear insight matters as much as engineering the pipeline.

In practice, you will be the team's data sherpa — the person who knows the data terrain cold, guides analysts and business partners through it, and turns an ambiguous “can we find out X?” into a trusted, well-modeled answer. You own the map — the definitions, lineage, and the “why” behind the numbers — as much as the pipelines.

This is an analytics-engineering role on a semi-business team. It is not a pure platform / infrastructure position — if your passion is exclusively distributed-systems plumbing with little interest in modeling, analysis, or guiding the business, this will not be the right fit.

Responsibilities Include:

Modeling & architecture — the core of the role

• Design and own the dimensional and semantic models — conformed dimensions, facts, star/snowflake schemas, slowly changing dimensions (Type 2), and well-defined grain — that serve as the trusted source of truth.

• Architect data marts spanning operational, advertising, and telemetry domains for analytics, reporting, AI, and operational use.

• Establish shared definitions and a semantic / metrics layer so users, sessions, devices, content, campaigns, and impressions mean the same thing everywhere.

SQL & analysis

• Write and optimize sophisticated analytical SQL — window functions, cohort and funnel logic, sessionization, distributions — on large event-scale datasets.

• Analyze complex datasets to find patterns, quantify drivers, and produce actionable insight; define new metrics and KPIs (usage, revenue, etc.) and the logic behind them.

• Independently investigate variance across platforms and communicate findings clearly to peers and senior leadership.

Business partnership

• Be the go-to guide for the data — the person who knows where every number comes from, what it means, and its quirks and landmines.

• Own the institutional knowledge of the data — definitions, lineage, and the reasoning behind metrics — and make it legible so analysts, ad ops, product, and finance can self-serve with confidence.

• Partner with stakeholders and source-system owners to translate ambiguous business questions into durable data models and metrics, and support/conduct strategic investigations and analysis.

Pipelines, quality & delivery

• Build and harmonize the ingestion and transformation pipelines — event data from client apps, ad-tech platforms, stitchers, ad servers, and telemetry — that feed the models, handling deduplication, late-arriving data, sessionization, and schema evolution.

• Stitch identity and sessions across client, server, and ad-side events for accurate user, content, and revenue analytics.

• Establish data-quality standards (testing, monitoring, alerting, freshness and volume SLAs) and troubleshoot incidents end-to-end — from a dashboard anomaly back through marts, transformations, and raw logs.

• Support and improve BI dashboards; document datasets, lineage, and business logic so the data map stays trustworthy and current.

• Mentor engineers and analysts on SQL, modeling, event data, and engineering best practices.

Basic Qualifications

• Expert SQL, including analytical SQL craft (window functions, complex joins, cohort / funnel / sessionization logic) and performance tuning on large event-scale datasets.

• Deep data-modeling expertise — dimensional modeling, star/snowflake schemas, slowly changing dimensions, conformed dimensions, grain, and data-mart design; able to design a trusted source of truth from messy multi-source data.

About Us

Slalom is a purpose-led, global business and technology consulting company. From strategy to implementation, our approach is fiercely human. In six+ countries and 43+ markets, we deeply understand our customers—and their customers—to deliver practical, end-to-end solutions that drive meaningful impact. Backed by close partnerships with over 400 leading technology providers, our 10,000+ strong team helps people and organizations dream bigger, move faster, and build better tomorrows for all. We’re honored to be consistently recognized as a great place to work, including being one of Fortune’s 100 Best Companies to Work For seven years running. Learn more at Slalom.com.

About the Role

Slalom’s Enhance & Operate (E&O) team is looking for a hands-on Data Engineer who enjoys building and improving data pipelines and keeping production platforms running smoothly. In this role, you’ll support a modern Databricks + Snowflake + Azure Data Factory (ADF) Enterprise Data Warehouse (EDW) ecosystem, combining data engineering fundamentals with operational excellence—monitoring pipelines, resolving incidents, developing code enhancements, and continuously improving reliability and performance in a service-oriented environment. 

You’ll work with a highly collaborative, cross-regional delivery model (“all-shore”) and partner closely with both technical and non-technical stakeholders. 

 

Work schedule: This role is working a shift between approximately 12:00 AM – 9:00 AM Central Time (CT).

 

What You’ll Do 
• Build, enhance, and troubleshoot Azure Data Factory (ADF) pipelines and Snowflake ELT/ETL processes, and Databricks ELT/ETL. 
• Monitor daily/weekly/monthly data batch cycles and respond quickly to job failures, latency, or data-quality issues. 
• Diagnose and resolve production incidents within Service-Level Agreements (SLA) targets using SQL, Python, platform logs, documentation, and runbooks. 
• Perform root cause analysis (RCA), write documentation of findings, and implement fixes to prevent recurrence of issues. 
• Drive operational improvements: automation, alert tuning, performance optimization, and reliability enhancements. 
• Work within ITIL/ITSM workflows (ticketing, incident/problem management, change processes) and communicate clearly with both technical and business stakeholders. 
• Collaborate with teammates across regions—sharing context early, documenting decisions, and maintaining strong handoffs. 
• Apply agentic AI in day-to-day E&O delivery using Snowflake Cortex and agentic coding tools to investigate incidents, accelerate root cause analysis, navigate code and data context, automate repeatable work, and turn operational knowledge into reusable skills. 
• Use agentic tools to support, not replace, engineering judgment by verifying evidence, challenging recommendations, protecting production data, and clearly communicating what the agent did, what was validated, and what still requires human approval. 

 

What You Bring 
• A proactive, data platform service-focused mindset: you will own incidents, issues, and development work end-to-end and follow your work through to resolution. 
• A Problem-solving mindset; Willingness to learn and understand how issues and resolutions fit into the EDW system design 
• Experience in working independently on assigned work; but also, comfortable collaborating with others to investigate and resolve issues; comfortable sharing concepts and information about issue resolution with teammates 
• 2-3 years of experience in data engineering, ETL/ELT development, or production support for data platforms. 
• Strong SQL skills (debugging, performance awareness, data validation). 
• Strong Python skills (troubleshooting, scripting, automation). 
• Hands-on experience with Snowflake and/or Databricks and Azure Data Factory (ADF). 
• Comfort working in a fast-paced, consulting-oriented environment where priorities shift and outcomes matter. 
• An agentic-assisted engineering mindset: comfort using AI agents as part of daily engineering work by providing clear context and constraints, reviewing proposed plans, SQL, and code, validating outputs against source evidence, and iterating when results are incomplete or unsafe. Prior Snowflake Cortex experience is not required. 
• Strong engineering fundamentals for AI-enabled operations, including Git and pull-request practices, scripting or Python experience, API and integration literacy, and the ability to trace issues across data pipelines, logs, code repositories, and operational records. 

 

Nice to have 
• Experience with ServiceNow, Control-M, Azure DevOps, Git-based workflows, and/or CI/CD. 
• Exposure to data observability/monitoring patterns, alerting, and platform logging. 
• Familiarity with modern data tooling (e.g., dbt) or cloud data ecosystem patterns. 
• Experience with Snowflake Cortex or enterprise GenAI platforms, including Cortex Agents, Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst, LLM functions, or a comparable enterprise agent or GenAI platform. 
• Experience building reusable agent solutions, including agent skills, tool integrations, prompts, or automations for repeatable engineering and operations workflows. 
• Experience with responsible AI operations, including retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) or governed knowledge, evaluation and observability, access controls, human-in-the-loop approvals, and safe production rollout. 

 

What success looks like (first 3–6 months) 
• You can independently troubleshoot common ADF/Snowflake/Databricks failures and stabilize recurring issues. 
• You consistently meet incident response expectations and communicate status clearly. 
• You deliver at least a few measurable improvements (automation, reduced failures, faster recovery, better monitoring). 
• You’re a trusted partner to teammates and stakeholders—reliable, proactive, and collaborative. 

Compensation and Benefits

Slalom prides itself on helping team members thrive in their work and life. As a result, Slalom is proud to invest in benefits that include meaningful time off and paid holidays, 401(k) with a match, a range of choices for highly subsidized health, dental, & vision coverage, adoption and fertility assistance, and long-term disability. We also offer yearly $350 reimbursement account for any well-being-related expenses.

Slalom is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. For this position, the base salary pay range is $30-35/hr. Actual compensation will depend upon an individual’s skills, experience, qualifications, location, and other relevant factors. The salary pay range is subject to change and may be modified at any time.

EEO and Accommodations

for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. Duration: Project Based Contract Through End of Year with Likely Extension

About the Role

Slalom’s Enhance & Operate (E&O) team is looking for a hands-on Data Engineer who enjoys building and improving data pipelines and keeping production platforms running smoothly. In this role, you’ll support a modern Databricks + Snowflake + Azure Data Factory (ADF) Enterprise Data Warehouse (EDW) ecosystem, combining data engineering fundamentals with operational excellence—monitoring pipelines, resolving incidents, developing code enhancements, and continuously improving reliability and performance in a service-oriented environment. 

You’ll work with a highly collaborative, cross-regional delivery model (“all-shore”) and partner closely with both technical and non-technical stakeholders. 

 

Work schedule: This role is working a shift between approximately 12:00 AM – 9:00 AM Central Time (CT).

 

What You’ll Do 
• Build, enhance, and troubleshoot Azure Data Factory (ADF) pipelines and Snowflake ELT/ETL processes, and Databricks ELT/ETL. 
• Monitor daily/weekly/monthly data batch cycles and respond quickly to job failures, latency, or data-quality issues. 
• Diagnose and resolve production incidents within Service-Level Agreements (SLA) targets using SQL, Python, platform logs, documentation, and runbooks. 
• Perform root cause analysis (RCA), write documentation of findings, and implement fixes to prevent recurrence of issues. 
• Drive operational improvements: automation, alert tuning, performance optimization, and reliability enhancements. 
• Work within ITIL/ITSM workflows (ticketing, incident/problem management, change processes) and communicate clearly with both technical and business stakeholders. 
• Collaborate with teammates across regions—sharing context early, documenting decisions, and maintaining strong handoffs. 
• Apply agentic AI in day-to-day E&O delivery using Snowflake Cortex and agentic coding tools to investigate incidents, accelerate root cause analysis, navigate code and data context, automate repeatable work, and turn operational knowledge into reusable skills. 
• Use agentic tools to support, not replace, engineering judgment by verifying evidence, challenging recommendations, protecting production data, and clearly communicating what the agent did, what was validated, and what still requires human approval. 

 

What You Bring 
• A proactive, data platform service-focused mindset: you will own incidents, issues, and development work end-to-end and follow your work through to resolution. 
• A Problem-solving mindset; Willingness to learn and understand how issues and resolutions fit into the EDW system design 
• Experience in working independently on assigned work; but also, comfortable collaborating with others to investigate and resolve issues; comfortable sharing concepts and information about issue resolution with teammates 
• 2-3 years of experience in data engineering, ETL/ELT development, or production support for data platforms. 
• Strong SQL skills (debugging, performance awareness, data validation). 
• Strong Python skills (troubleshooting, scripting, automation). 
• Hands-on experience with Snowflake and/or Databricks and Azure Data Factory (ADF). 
• Comfort working in a fast-paced, consulting-oriented environment where priorities shift and outcomes matter. 
• An agentic-assisted engineering mindset: comfort using AI agents as part of daily engineering work by providing clear context and constraints, reviewing proposed plans, SQL, and code, validating outputs against source evidence, and iterating when results are incomplete or unsafe. Prior Snowflake Cortex experience is not required. 
• Strong engineering fundamentals for AI-enabled operations, including Git and pull-request practices, scripting or Python experience, API and integration literacy, and the ability to trace issues across data pipelines, logs, code repositories, and operational records. 

 

Nice to have 
• Experience with ServiceNow, Control-M, Azure DevOps, Git-based workflows, and/or CI/CD. 
• Exposure to data observability/monitoring patterns, alerting, and platform logging. 
• Familiarity with modern data tooling (e.g., dbt) or cloud data ecosystem patterns. 
• Experience with Snowflake Cortex or enterprise GenAI platforms, including Cortex Agents, Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst, LLM functions, or a comparable enterprise agent or GenAI platform. 
• Experience building reusable agent solutions, including agent skills, tool integrations, prompts, or automations for repeatable engineering and operations workflows.

title: Principal Data Engineer
description:
At T-Mobile, we invest in YOU! Our Total Rewards Package ensures that employees get the same big love we give our customers. All team members receive a competitive base salary and compensation package - this is Total Rewards. Employees enjoy multiple wealth-building opportunities through our annual stock grant, employee stock purchase plan, 401(k), and access to free, year-round money coaches. That’s how we’re UNSTOPPABLE for our employees!

Job Overview

We're looking for a Principal Data Engineer who brings strong technical judgment, a product-oriented mindset, and the ability to own data solutions end-to-end—from architecture and modeling to implementation and delivery—in a dynamic AdTech environment. You'll join a fast paced team that builds, runs, and operates the T-Mobile Advertising Solutions (T-Ads) platforms, including our audience building, rideshare, and retail media network solutions. This is a product used by all the major advertising agencies and many top consumer product brands in the United States.

This role leads the development and implementation of data pipelines critical to organizational data infrastructure and analytics capabilities. You'll combine technical leadership with hands-on contributions to achieve data engineering initiatives. If you thrive on collaborating with multi-functional teams to solve complex data challenges, designing scalable data architectures, and deploying robust data pipelines to the cloud, we want to talk to you!

Job Responsibilities:

• Lead the design and development of data warehouse and business analytics solutions to ensure scalable and reliable data infrastructure

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to analyze and architect data solutions that meet business requirements

• Research and recommend technical approaches to address complex data migration, development, and integration challenges

• Provide hands-on leadership in data implementation projects and manage independent workstreams to deliver project objectives

• Facilitate workshops and design sessions to build relationships and align data engineering efforts with organizational goals

• Mentor data engineers to develop their skills in data architecture and engineering practices

• Assist team management in defining projects, including helping estimate, plan and scope work and other duties/projects as assigned by business management as needed

Education and Work Experience:

• Bachelor's Degree plus 7 years of related work experience OR Advanced degree with 5 years of related experience (Required)

• Acceptable areas of study include Mathematics, Computer Science, Engineering, Finance, Statistics, or related technical field (Required)

• 7-10 years Related experience as a Data Engineer (Required)

• 5+ years developing cloud solutions using data services (Required)

• Minimum 3+ years of managing or leading/coaching data engineering teams (Required)

• Experience designing and building self-service analytics and big data solutions using cloud technologies (e.g., EMR, Aurora, Redshift, Glue, S3, SWF, Quicksight etc.) (Required)

• Experience with the Software development Life Cycle (SDLC) and Agile/Scrum methods (Preferred)

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

• Cloud Computing (Required)

• Collaboration (Required)

• Data Architecture (Required)

• Data Engineering (Required)

• Databricks DBRX (Required)

• Engineering Leadership (Required)

• Project Scoping (Required)

• Snowflake (Platform) (Required)

Licenses and Certifications:

• Cloud platform certification(s) (AWS Certified Solutions Architect, AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner, OR Microsoft Certified Solutions Associate (MCSA) (Required)

• At least 18 years of age

• Legally authorized to work in the United States

Travel:

Travel Required (Yes/No): No

DOT Regulated:

DOT Regulated Position (Yes/No): No

Safety Sensitive Position (Yes/No): No

Base Pay Range: $125,600 - $226,600

Corporate Bonus Target: 20%

We cover all of the bases, offering medical, dental and vision insurance, a flexible spending account, 401(k), employee stock grants, employee stock purchase plan, paid time off and up to 12 paid holidays - which total about 4 weeks for new full-time employees and about 2.5 weeks for new part-time employees annually - paid parental and family leave, family building benefits, back-up care, enhanced family support, childcare subsidy, tuition assistance, college coaching, short- and long-term disability, voluntary AD&D coverage, voluntary accident coverage, voluntary life insurance, voluntary disability insurance, and voluntary long-term care insurance. We don't stop there - eligible employees can also receive mobile service & home internet discounts, pet insurance, and access to commuter and transit programs! To learn about T-Mobile’s amazing benefits, check out www.t-mobilebenefits.com.

title: Data Center Technician
description:
Data Center Technician

Join the Team Powering the World's Most Advanced Cloud Infrastructure

Are you passionate about technology, hands-on problem solving, and working behind the scenes of one of the largest cloud platforms in the world? Our client is seeking motivated Data Center Technicians to help support critical infrastructure that powers millions of users globally. This is an exciting opportunity to work in a fast-paced, cutting-edge data center environment where you'll gain exposure to enterprise networking, hardware deployment, troubleshooting, and large-scale infrastructure projects.
What You'll Do

As a Data Center Technician, you'll play a key role in supporting infrastructure deployments and ensuring our client's data center operations run efficiently and reliably.
Installation & Deployment
• Upgrade and install RNG devices within a data center environment.
• Prepare, stage, configure, install, and decommission hardware including servers, switches, racks, and storage devices.
• Perform startup and shutdown procedures using established checklists, deployment guides, and standard operating procedures.
• Support technology refresh projects, including memory upgrades and operating system rebuilds.
Network Connectivity & Infrastructure
• Collaborate closely with Network Engineers to validate Layer 1 connectivity and provision switches and routers.
• Verify network ports, cabling, and device connections to ensure proper functionality.
• Perform post-deployment quality checks to ensure grounding, labeling, staging, and cabling meet clients standards and safety requirements.
Troubleshooting & Break/Fix Support
• Diagnose hardware and connectivity issues using established troubleshooting procedures.
• Perform break/fix activities by identifying root causes and replacing defective server and networking components.
• Escalate incidents and technical issues appropriately while following operational procedures.
Operational Excellence & Safety
• Conduct daily safety inspections and equipment checks to maintain a safe working environment.
• Ensure all work is completed according to deployment standards, safety protocols, and network design requirements.
• Maintain accurate documentation and provide regular project and status updates to Microsoft stakeholders.
What Makes This Role Exciting?
• Work inside one of the world's largest and most advanced cloud data center environments.
• Gain hands-on experience with enterprise-class servers, networking equipment, and critical infrastructure.
• Partner with highly skilled engineers and technology professionals
• Build valuable experience in networking, hardware deployment, troubleshooting, and data center operations.
Ideal Candidate

We're looking for individuals who:
• Enjoy hands-on technical work and problem-solving.
• Have data center experience working with hardware, cabling, networking, or IT infrastructure.
• Can follow detailed processes and procedures with precision.
• Thrive in fast-paced, team-oriented environments.
• Communicate effectively with clients, engineers, and project teams.
• Prioritize safety, quality, and operational excellence.
Job Type & Location

This is a Contract position based out of Ashburn, VA.
Pay and Benefits

The pay range for this position is $25.00 - $25.00/hr.

classification and length of employment. Benefits are subject to change and may be
